status: PRE-REGISTERED: committed before the corroboration module, its replay and its tests existed, and before html5lib parsed any fixture. Not edited after results are seen; post-run notes go to REPORT.md.
scope: structural evidence for triage of one explicit Sphinx API id in original public HTML bytes; not admission, not a new extractor or router, not a claim that two parsers establish source truth

selection_rule.use: imported read-only; select_unit() keeps the conservative policy on the lxml side; its rule is mirrored for both trees

pins.wheels: wheels/WHEELS.json and wheels/requirements.lock (html5lib 1.1, six 1.17.0, webencodings 0.5.1), verified by scripts/verify_wheels.py
pins.lxml: not retained (native); the replay requires an existing lxml and records its version; Linux evidence: lxml 6.1.3, libxml2 2.14.6

parsers.lxml: lxml.html.document_fromstring(original_bytes, parser=lxml.html.HTMLParser()) with its defaults, exactly as anchor_unit.select_unit(); diagnostics = the complete ordered parser.error_log
parsers.html5lib: html5lib.HTMLParser(tree=html5lib.getTreeBuilder('etree'), strict=False, namespaceHTMLElements=True, debug=False).parse(original_bytes, override_encoding=None, transport_encoding=None, useChardet=False, scripting=False); getTreeBuilder('etree') uses the stdlib xml.etree.ElementTree with fullTree=False, so parse() returns the html element; diagnostics = the complete ordered parser.errors ((line, col), code, datavars)

decoding_policy: both parsers receive the complete original bytes, never a fragment and never re-encoded bytes. lxml/libxml2 choose the encoding themselves (docinfo.encoding). html5lib 1.1 checks a BOM first, then override_encoding (None here), transport_encoding (None), a meta prescan of the first 1024 bytes, then the windows-1252 default; useChardet=False disables the optional chardet guess. The two choices are compared by codecs.lookup(name).name; any disagreement is a REVIEW finding; nothing is rewritten.
name_mapping: html5lib/ElementTree tags are '{http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml}<local>' for HTML elements; the comparison maps exactly that namespace to <local>. lxml.html tags have no namespace and are used as they are. Elements in any other namespace keep their full '{ns}local' tag and never match dt/dd/dl/a. ElementTree comments (tag is xml.etree.ElementTree.Comment) and processing instructions are kind comment/pi; lxml _Comment/_ProcessingInstruction likewise.
selection_rule: the anchor_unit.py rule, applied to each tree: every element whose id attribute equals the anchor exactly (no NFC, no percent-decoding) is listed; exactly one must exist (otherwise MISSING_ID, ID_NORMALIZATION_MISMATCH or DUPLICATE_ID, and no unit is chosen); it must be a dt whose class has 'sig' and 'sig-object' with a dl parent; the unit is the maximal run of dt siblings containing it plus the following run of dd siblings, each whole; MULTIPLE_GROUPS_IN_OBJECT_DL, STRAY_CONTENT_IN_OBJECT_DL, NO_DESCRIPTION, EMPTY_DESCRIPTION, UNEXPECTED_NESTED_OBJECT as in anchor_unit.py. Structural reasons exclude PARSER_DIAGNOSTICS_PRESENT, which is reported with the diagnostics.
text_rule: text(element) = element.text + for each child in order: text(child) + child.tail, where text(comment or pi) = '' (its data is excluded, its tail kept). unit text = for each top-level unit element i: text(element_i) + tail_i if i is not the last; the last element's tail is excluded. No normalisation. Checked, not assumed, against lxml text_content() (via select_unit) and against ElementTree itertext().
disposition_rule: STRUCTURE_CORROBORATED only if: no lxml diagnostic, no html5lib error, the same encoding, exactly one exact match in each tree, no structural reason in either tree, and identical membership (signature ids, counts), boundaries, topology, links and unit text (exact string). Anything else is REVIEW. Neither value is admission: consumers get no permission from this experiment, and the whole-unit byte count does not imply that any caller's final prompt fits; nothing is truncated.
required_properties: R1 both parsers parse the complete original bytes: the report's sha256/bytes equal the file's
R2 complete ordered lxml error_log (equal to the helper's) and complete ordered html5lib errors, every available field, no line filtering or suppression
R3 all exact id matches listed per tree; more than one gives no unit; no first-match selection
R4 encodings, versions and every parser option recorded; encoding disagreement is REVIEW
R5 unit membership, boundaries, ordered topology and links per tree, with the explicit name mapping
R6 exact unit text, its UTF-8 size and sha256 per tree, by the text rule; rule text equals helper text_content (lxml) and itertext (html5lib), recorded as checks
R7 comparison findings separate from the triage disposition; REVIEW retained whenever diagnostics, ambiguity or disagreement remain
R8 no key matching forbidden_report_keys anywhere in a report; no serialization search, no lexical id count, no text normalisation
R9 the existing helper's reasons and status are reported unchanged (conservative policy preserved)
